entry.title: Add more spec_urls; set some standard_tracks to false (APIs A-C)
entry.content:
This is a bit of a test PR to see if we could add spec_urls everywhere (especially for behavioral sub features).
Some things came up where we should probably agree on spec_url consistency for a few common sub features:

  • worker_support
  • iterable sub features (forEach, keys, values, iterator, etc)
  • secure_context_required
    I decided to use the spec_url for the interface itself, happy to hear other thoughts.

Also, I think when a sub aspect of e.g. a method is described then it is okay to link to the same spec section as the method. So, basically the sub feature gets the same spec_url as the parent feature.

I marked standard_track false for a few things: CSSPrimitiveValue, CSSValue, CSSValueList. Doesn't look like these will be going anywhere.

entry.title: Chrome 95 / FF 128 add script-closeability depending on opener
entry.content:
Summary

As discussed in Mozilla Bug 1316857 comment 18, the concept of "same script" is vague and likely inaccurate.

Additionally, to determine script-closeability, browsers switched from 'has an opener' to 'was opened by script' and that might be useful to note.

Test results and supporting details

https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1316857#c18

Related issues

#9492

My perception is these notes are usually quite short. Script-closeability also depends on the session history, so something like "Before Chrome 95, scripts could only close windows that had an opener" would be incorrect. I tried to omit this detail, but am unsure whether that made my phrasing too awkward. We could remove the notes entirely. An alternative phrasing might be "Before Chrome 95, whether a window could be closed by script depended on having an opener, not on whether it was created by web content."
